message.content:
The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands. In general:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| **Red blood cells** (which lack mitochondria) | 0 |
| **Neurons** (high energy demand) | ~1–2 × 10⁴ per neuron |
| **Skeletal muscle fibers** (very high energy demand) | ~5–10 × 10⁴ per fiber |
| **Liver hepatocytes** (moderate energy demand) | ~1–5 × 10³ per cell |
| **Epithelial cells** (moderate energy demand) | ~200–500 per cell |
| **Stem cells** (low energy demand) | ~50–200 per cell |

These numbers are approximate averages; actual counts can differ by an order of magnitude within a given tissue or under different physiological conditions.
